memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support rolling: Selectins mediate transient endothelial sticking; E-selectin is induced by IL-1/TNF, P-selectin mobilized by histamine/thrombin, and L-selectin expressed on leukocytes.
Original page image and extracted text support firm adhesion: Activated leukocyte integrins bind endothelial ligands: LFA-1 and Mac-1 to ICAM-1, VLA-4 to VCAM-1.
Original page image and extracted text support transmigration: PECAM-1/CD31 is present on leukocytes and endothelial cells; leukocyte collagenases degrade basement membrane.

Original page image and extracted text support contraction versus retraction: Histamine, bradykinins and leukotrienes produce immediate transient venular gaps; TNF/IL-1-mediated cytoskeletal retraction is delayed. Both are reversible.

Original page image and extracted text support direct injury: Severe direct endothelial injury causes immediate sustained leakage in arterioles/capillaries/venules; mild injury causes delayed prolonged leakage in capillaries/venules.
Original page image and extracted text support transcytosis: VEGF induces vesicular transport through venular endothelial cells.
Original page image and extracted text support new vessels: Angiogenic vessels can leak until intercellular junctions form.

Original page image and extracted text support protein escape: Protein escape decreases intravascular osmotic pressure and increases interstitial osmotic pressure; dilation increases hydrostatic pressure, promoting edema.
Original page image and extracted text support transudation: Low-protein plasma ultrafiltration driven by increased hydrostatic pressure.
Original page image and extracted text support exudation: Protein-rich fluid escape driven by increased vascular permeability.
Original page image and extracted text support directional migration: Chemotaxis follows a chemical gradient toward injury; bacterial products, C5a, LTB4 and chemokines are listed attractants.
Original page image and extracted text support chemokine targets: IL-8 attracts neutrophils; eotaxin eosinophils; MCP-1/MIP-1alpha monocytes; RANTES lymphocytes and monocytes.
Original page image and extracted text support stimulus and cells: Neutrophils predominate in early acute inflammation; eosinophils in allergy/parasitic infestation; lymphocytes in viral infection.
Original page image and extracted text support entry stages: Recognition/attachment precedes pseudopod engulfment and fusion of the phagocytic vacuole with lysosomes.
Original page image and extracted text support opsonin recognition: The illustration shows antibody-Fc receptor and C3b-C3b receptor recognition of coated bacteria, plus C-reactive protein coating.

Original page image and extracted text support oxidative killing: NADPH oxidase generates reactive oxygen species; neutrophil myeloperoxidase uses H2O2 in the presence of chloride during microbial killing.

memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support degradation: Acid hydrolases degrade material following microbial killing.
Original page image and extracted text support adhesion: LAD-1 involves LFA-1/Mac-1 integrin subunit defects; LAD-2 lacks sialyl-Lewis X that binds E/P-selectin.

Original page image and extracted text support trafficking: Chediak-Higashi syndrome involves a microtubule assembly defect with impaired locomotion and lysosomal degranulation; inheritance is autosomal recessive.

memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support oxidative defense: NADPH oxidase deficiency impairs superoxide generation and oxygen-dependent killing in chronic granulomatous disease.
Original page image and extracted text support cyclooxygenase: Prostaglandins are arachidonic acid derivatives produced through cyclooxygenase; inflammatory effects include pain and fever.
Original page image and extracted text support platelets and tone: PGI2 dilates vessels and inhibits platelet aggregation; TXA2 constricts vessels and promotes aggregation.
Original page image and extracted text support leukotriene separation: LTB4 promotes neutrophil chemotaxis; LTC4/LTD4/LTE4 promote bronchospasm and increased vascular permeability.

memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support lipoxins: LXA4/LXB4 inhibit neutrophil adhesion and chemotaxis.
Original page image and extracted text support histamine: Stored in mast cells, platelets and basophils; promotes vasodilation and increased permeability.

Original page image and extracted text support paf: Generated from membrane phospholipids through phospholipase A2; stimulates platelets and promotes leukocyte adhesion, chemotaxis, degranulation and oxidative burst.

Original page image and extracted text support endothelial no: Acetylcholine and bradykinin stimulate endothelial release of short-acting nitric oxide, producing vasodilation and inhibition of platelet aggregation.

memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support bradykinin: Activated factor XII forms kallikrein from prekallikrein; kallikrein cleaves kininogen to bradykinin, which causes pain, permeability, vasodilation and bronchial constriction.
Original page image and extracted text support plasmin: Factor XII activation connects to plasmin formation; plasmin activates complement.

Original page image and extracted text support complement functions: C3a/C5a: vascular effects and mast-cell degranulation; C5a: chemotaxis/integrin avidity; C3b/C3bi: opsonization; terminal MAC: membrane injury/lysis.
Original page image and extracted text support determinants: Severity of tissue damage, regenerative capacity and injurious-agent type determine the outcome.
Original page image and extracted text support resolution: Limited or brief injury with minimal damage and replacement capacity favors resolution.
Original page image and extracted text support abscess: Failure to eliminate pyogenic infection can produce liquefaction and pus.

Original page image and extracted text support fibrosis and persistence: Substantial destruction, nonregenerating tissues or unabsorbed fibrinous exudate favor fibrosis; persistent injury can lead to chronic inflammation.
Original page image and extracted text support serous: Relatively low-cell, low-protein fluid can accumulate in serous inflammation, as in skin blisters.

memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support fibrinous: Plasma fibrinogen exudes and becomes deposited tissue fibrin.
Original page image and extracted text support suppurative: A neutrophil-rich exudate; pus combines viable/dead neutrophils, necrotic tissue and edema fluid.
Original page image and extracted text support ulceration: Necrosis/erosion of an epithelial surface; layers include neutrophilic exudate, vascular proliferation and proliferating fibroblasts.
Original page image and extracted text support m1: Microbes/IFN-gamma induce classical activation: ROS/NO/lysosomal enzymes support killing; IL-1/IL-12/IL-23/chemokines support inflammation.
Original page image and extracted text support m2: IL-4/IL-13 induce alternative activation: growth factors/TGF-beta support repair/fibrosis; IL-10/TGF-beta support anti-inflammatory effects.
Original page image and extracted text support resolution: Macrophages clear excess fluid, apoptotic neutrophils and debris during resolution.
Original page image and extracted text support antigen presentation: Macrophages present antigen fragments to activate lymphocytes.
Original page image and extracted text support forward signal: Activated lymphocytes produce IFN-gamma that activates macrophages.

Original page image and extracted text support feedback: Macrophages release IL-1/TNF, further activating lymphocytes and other cells; reciprocal stimulation persists until antigen removal or modulation.
Original page image and extracted text support granulation tissue: New blood vessels, inflammatory cells, fibroblasts and collagen repair injured tissue by fibrous replacement.
Original page image and extracted text support granuloma: An aggregate of activated epithelioid macrophages can eradicate organisms or wall off degradation-resistant particles.
Original page image and extracted text support etiologies: Examples include bacterial, fungal and parasitic infections, inorganic dusts, foreign bodies, and unknown causes such as sarcoidosis.

memorize.finding: Original page image and extracted text support cytokine sequence: TNF induces IL-1, which stimulates IL-6.
Original page image and extracted text support fever: TNF/IL-1 stimulate prostaglandin production at the thermoregulatory center.
Original page image and extracted text support organ responses: IL-6 stimulates hepatic plasma proteins, mainly fibrinogen; IL-1/TNF increase marrow leukocyte production.
Original page image and extracted text support cell pattern: Bacterial infection emphasizes PMNs, parasites with allergy eosinophils, and viral infection lymphocytes.
